description: Single-panel line/scatter plot showing deformation-induced martensitic transformation kinetics. Linear x-axis "True Strain" from 0.0 to 0.5 with major ticks every 0.1; linear y-axis "Martensite Fraction (%)" from 0 to 30 with gridlines every 5 units. Three labelled entries: "Exp.RD" = red open circles joined by a red line (tensile loading along rolling direction), "Exp.TD" = blue open circles joined by a blue line (transverse direction), and "Model" = black dashed lines (two dashed curves) fitted with the OC model. Both experimental curves start near zero martensite fraction below ~0.03 strain, then rise monotonically and accelerate strongly above ~0.15 strain. At every common strain the RD curve lies above the TD curve; the RD curve reaches approximately the 25 % gridline and slightly exceeds it at the highest plotted strain (~0.48-0.5), while the TD curve ends at about 21 % near strain ~0.5. The two dashed model curves track the corresponding experimental sets closely at low strain but fall progressively below them at high strain, so the OC model under-predicts the martensite fraction in the large-strain regime for both directions. The figure demonstrates that, for identical strain, the same steel transforms to a larger martensite fraction under RD than under TD loading, i.e. the transformation kinetics is loading-direction dependent.

observations.observation: The plot axes are linear: x = 'True Strain' from 0.0 to 0.5 (ticks every 0.1), y = 'Martensite Fraction (%)' from 0 to 30 (gridlines every 5).
The legend contains three entries: 'Exp.RD' (red open circles), 'Exp.TD' (blue open circles) and 'Model' (black dashed line).
The experimental RD curve lies above the experimental TD curve at every common true strain value.
The Exp.RD data reach approximately the 25 % gridline and slightly exceed it at the highest plotted strain (near 0.48-0.5), whereas Exp.TD ends at about 21 % near strain 0.5.
Both experimental curves are near zero below about 0.03 true strain and accelerate strongly above roughly 0.15 strain, giving a sigmoidal shape.

The black dashed model curves fall progressively below the experimental points at high strain while lying close to (or slightly above) them at low strain, so the OC model under-predicts the martensite fraction in the large-strain regime for both directions.
The caption states that the dashed lines are fitted curves based on the OC model.
The caption states the figure shows deformation-induced martensitic transformation kinetics of the steel in two tensile directions.
The citing text states the initial austenite fraction F_gamma0 is 46.5 vol.%.
The citing text states martensite nucleation is assumed random with n = 2 in the OC model.

The citing text states the OC model was first fitted to the TD sample and the resulting parameters then applied to the RD sample with plastic strain relation epsilon_RD = 1.15 epsilon_TD, determined from micro-DIC data (Fig. 12(c) and (d)).
The citing text concludes that loading-direction-dependent strain distribution plays a key role in the kinetics of strain-induced martensite transformation.
Fig. 14 is presented as evidence of the accuracy of the OC model in predicting martensite fraction compared with HEXRD experimental data.

subfigures.description: Martensite fraction (%) versus true strain (0.0-0.5). Red open circles (Exp.RD) and blue open circles (Exp.TD) are experimental HEXRD-derived data; black dashed lines are OC-model fits. Exp.RD exceeds Exp.TD at all shared strains, reaching about 25 % at ~0.48 strain versus about 21 % for Exp.TD at ~0.5 strain. Both dashed fits lie below the experimental data at high strain.
